reasons.clean_text: Paper A mentions code/test_lib.py and commit hashes in the body (page 3) and has an odd remark that it knows Chen et al. only by title (page 2); Paper B is worse, with paper/aux_numbers.py in the body (page 4), REPRODUCE.md mentions, script paths in captions and code-like cap names (emp99, ceil) throughout.
reasons.abstract_intro: Paper A's abstract is dense and long but gives a well-structured contribution list and positions itself in social choice (pages 1-2); Paper B's abstract is more concise and its related work is solid (pages 1-2), so the two are roughly even here.

reasons.title: The titles are nearly identical and both long. A's 'Minimum Investment Under Different Aggregation Rules' (p1) is slightly tighter than B's 'Minimum-Investment Analysis Across Aggregation Rules' (p1), so the two are about even.
reasons.figure1: Neither paper has a mechanism diagram. A's Figure 1 (p5) is a clean two-board, three-panel plot of feasibility and cost with bootstrap bands. B's Figure 1 (p5) is a busy 3x3 grid of jagged lines with eight rules that is harder to read.
reasons.figures_tables: A's figures and tables share one consistent style (pp5-7, 11-16). B has an almost unreadable miniature left panel in Figure 5 (p12) and an empty 'Appendix B Additional results' heading (p10), though its booktabs tables (pp4, 13-15) are clean.
reasons.experiments: Both are rich. A covers two boards, a cap family, exact checks against solvers, noise and task bootstrap, task-count scaling and many sensitivity variants (pp4-7, 10-16). B adds a third board, Holm-corrected paired tests, a synthetic latent-factor study and a case study (pp4-8), which roughly balances A.
reasons.page_use: Both bodies fill about 8-9 pages. A's main text runs to p9 with 13 references; B's main text ends on p8 with about 19 references, so both are adequate.
reasons.clean_text: Both leak pipeline details. A puts 'Generated by figures/src/...py' in most captions and cites 'paper/aux_numbers.py' in the body (p4). B cites 'code/test_lib.py' in the body (p3), 'code/02_main.py' (p11), HTTP 429 and LLM-agent talk in the appendix (p10), and gives incorrect checklist answers (p19).
reasons.abstract_intro: A's abstract (p1) is concise and its introduction and related work (pp1-2) are well positioned. B's abstract (p1) is long at 29 lines, though its contributions list and social-choice related work (p2) are solid.

reasons.title: Paper A's title (page 1) is concise and specific, while Paper B's two-part question title (page 1) is long and wordy, so A is better here.
reasons.figure1: Paper A's Figure 1 (page 5) is a clean two-panel budget–success CDF that is easy to read; Paper B's Figure 1 (page 5) is a dense six-panel plot with overlapping shaded bands; neither is a mechanism or overview diagram.
reasons.figures_tables: Paper A's figures and tables (pages 4–7, 11–13) are consistent and uncluttered; Paper B's (pages 5–7, 11–16) are informative but crowded, use small fonts in Tables 1–2, and end captions with script names.
reasons.experiments: Paper B is richer and better aligned with the task: three cost measures (L1, K, L∞), five or more rules, data-grounded and oracle caps, closed-form propositions checked against solvers, bootstrap and evaluation-noise intervals, task-count scaling and pre-registered hypotheses (pages 3–8); Paper A uses only a task-count cost with hypothetical ceilings, though it adds random baselines and pool checks.
reasons.page_use: Paper B's body fills about 8.5 pages up to its references on page 9, whereas Paper A's body ends early on page 8 with a short conclusion and a mostly blank page.
reasons.clean_text: Both papers leak pipeline details: Paper A puts a git commit hash and code/data/manifest.json in the body (page 3) and many file paths in Appendix C (page 14); Paper B names paper/aux_numbers.py in the body (page 4) and 'Generated by figures/src/...' in nearly every caption.
reasons.abstract_intro: Both abstracts are dense; Paper B's introduction (pages 1–2) states the question, contributions and findings more clearly and has a fuller related-work section with explicit positioning, while Paper A's hedged phrasing makes its message harder to follow.
